body:
Looks like this has breaking changes/regressions (see below). Tracking HEAD for a bit to see if some of these get fixed in the next patch release.

(Blocker for the matching luv bump with @lewis6991 meta annotation fixes.)

comment_regular_data.body:
Windows. This breaks Windows. 🙄 

```
libuv.lib(pipe.c.obj) : error LNK2001: unresolved external symbol WaitOnAddress

libuv.lib(pipe.c.obj) : error LNK2001: unresolved external symbol WakeByAddressSingle
```

do we have to add something new (`synchronization`?) to `target_link_libraries` somewhere? @dundargoc

_and_ macOS 😩 

```
FAILED   ...uild/Xtest_xdg_core/test/functional/core/server_spec.lua @ 388: startup --listen validates
Expected values to be equal.
Expected:
1
Actual:
0
stack traceback:
	...uild/Xtest_xdg_core/test/functional/core/server_spec.lua:375: in function '_test'
	...uild/Xtest_xdg_core/test/functional/core/server_spec.lua:406: in function <...uild/Xtest_xdg_core/test/functional/core/server_spec.lua:388>
```
(not a flake)

>   1. Windows needs synchronization linked. Libuv now calls WaitOnAddress and WakeByAddressSingle, which require that library. Add it to cmake/FindLibuv.cmake:44 and the Zig libuv package’s Windows dependencies. Linking only the Neovim executable would leave Zig’s test_nlua0 broken.
> 
>   2. The macOS test’s “too long” path is now valid. Libuv #5047 intentionally increased supported socket-path lengths. The test (test/functional/core/server_spec.lua:405) uses 207 bytes; macOS now supports up to 253. I verified that binding, retrieving the full name, and connecting all succeed without truncation. Changing
>      rep(192) to rep(256) makes the path genuinely too long.

> Add it to cmake/FindLibuv.cmake:44 and the Zig libuv package’s Windows dependencies.

Hmm, shouldn't that be in upstream CMake list? And the Zig part should probably be done at allyourcodebase/libuv (@bfredl)?

Thanks, but I'm fine to make that fix upstream (they haven't tagged 1.53.0 yet for that reason).

Also, I'm a bit unsure about the library name there ;) (Do we want to link statically or dynamically?)
Sure. Was just posting in the off chance it was useful in any capacity. It was low effort on my part.

Hmm, so it looks like Zig _does_ need the dynamic `ms_windows_what_happened_to_eight_characters_ought_to_be_enough_for_any_filename` dll, while CMake needs the statig `synchronization.lib` ?

@dundargoc
